story: UAF publishes the amount and mechanism of AURORA-AI, the only Alaska project on DOE's Genesis Mission list, at $725,000 with Cordova Electric Cooperative as a named partner

claims.claim: The University of Alaska Fairbanks received a $725,000 award from the U.S. Department of Energy for the AURORA-AI project.
claims.verbatim: $725,000 award from the U.S. Department of Energy.
claims.notes: Corroborated independently on the ACEP release, fetched separately, which carries the same figure. This is the awardee institution announcing its own award, so it is primary.

claims.claim: AURORA-AI stands for Alaska Utility Resilience and Optimization using Real-time AI.
claims.value: Alaska Utility Resilience and Optimization using Real-time AI
claims.verbatim: Alaska Utility Resilience and Optimization using Real-time AI
claims.notes: Same expansion appears on the ACEP release.

claims.claim: Richard Wies is the principal investigator for AURORA-AI.
claims.verbatim: Richard Wies, principal investigator for the project and a professor
claims.notes: Use principal investigator as the title on a slide. That is the part confirmed verbatim on both pages.

claims.claim: AURORA-AI is a partnership of the UAF Alaska Center for Energy and Power, Colorado State University, the National Laboratory of the Rockies and Cordova Electric Cooperative.
claims.verbatim: researchers from the UAF Alaska Center for Energy and Power, Colorado State University, the National Laboratory of the Rockies and Cordova Electric Cooperative
claims.notes: Identical partner list on the ACEP release.

claims.claim: UAF says AURORA-AI will combine high-resolution utility data, virtual replicas of the power grid and AI to forecast demand, detect abnormal operating conditions and optimize energy resources.
claims.value: virtual replicas of the power grid
claims.verbatim: AURORA-AI will combine high-resolution utility data, virtual replicas of the power grid and state-of-the-art AI to help utilities forecast demand, detect abnormal operating conditions, optimize energy resources
claims.notes: The mechanism sentence. Do not put the phrase digital twin inside quotation marks against this URL.

claims.claim: UAF says Alaska has over 200 remote microgrids.
claims.verbatim: With over 200 remote microgrids, Alaska is one of the ideal environments for microgrid research.
claims.notes: The wording is over 200, not a flat 200. Write it as over 200 or more than 200.

claims.claim: UAF published the AURORA-AI release on August 11th, 2026.
claims.notes: Byline Yuri Bult-Ito. Inside the run window.

claims.claim: The Alaska Center for Energy and Power published its own AURORA-AI release on the same day, August 11th, 2026.
claims.verbatim: UAF Leads AI Project to Strengthen Alaska's Rural Power Grids
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Center for Energy and Power, University of Alaska Fairbanks
claims.notes: Two separate URLs, same date and byline. This is the day the amount and the mechanism became public.

claims.claim: Richard Wies said Alaska's isolated power systems provide an ideal environment for developing and testing next-generation technologies that can improve electric grid resilience.
claims.value: Wies quote on isolated power systems
claims.verbatim: Alaska's isolated power systems provide an ideal environment for developing and testing next-generation technologies that can improve electric grid resilience," Wies said.
claims.notes: The only Wies quotation confirmed verbatim on a fetched page. Any other Wies line must not be set in quotation marks.

claims.claim: The AURORA-AI award was made under the U.S. Department of Energy's Genesis Mission.
claims.verbatim: U.S. Department of Energy's Genesis Mission
claims.notes: Named as the funding mechanism on both the UAF and ACEP releases.

claims.claim: The Department of Energy selected 278 projects in the first Genesis Mission round.
claims.verbatim: The 278 projects selected today represent the very best of our nation's scientific enterprise.
claims.notes: AURORA-AI is one of these 278.

claims.claim: Of the first round Genesis Mission projects, 168 are led by universities.
claims.verbatim: 168 led by universities
claims.notes: Sanity check passes, 168 is less than 278.

claims.claim: The first Genesis Mission round spans 342 participating institutions including 16 national laboratories and 142 universities.
claims.verbatim: 342 participating institutions: 16 DOE and NNSA National Laboratories, 142 universities, 157 companies, 13 nonprofit organizations, and 14 other institutions.
claims.notes: Components sum to 342. The verbatim carries a colon because the page prints one. Reader copy must not.

claims.claim: The Department of Energy announced the first selected Genesis Mission projects on July 22nd, 2026.
claims.notes: The earlier announcement that the August 11th release updates.

claims.claim: The $293 million Genesis Mission figure is the size of the Request for Application announced on March 17th, 2026 and the Department of Energy does not state it as the combined value of the 278 selected projects.
claims.verbatim: This includes a $293 million Request for Application (RFA), "The Genesis Mission: Transforming Science and Energy with AI."
claims.notes: Do not write $293 million for 278 projects on any slide. Safe phrasing is selected under a $293 million Request for Application.

claims.claim: Genesis Mission Phase I awards range from $500,000 to $750,000 and support a nine month project period.
claims.verbatim: Phase I awards will range from $500,000 to $750,000 and will support a nine month project period.
claims.notes: Shows the $725,000 is near the top of the published band and not a truncated number.

claims.claim: The $725,000 AURORA-AI award falls inside the published Genesis Mission Phase I band of $500,000 to $750,000.
claims.verbatim: Phase I awards will range from $500,000 to $750,000 and will support a nine month project period.
claims.notes: DERIVED arithmetic across C01 and C16. DOE has not confirmed AURORA-AI is a Phase I award, so hedge as consistent with the Phase I band rather than asserting the phase.

claims.claim: Greensparc delivered 170 kilowatts of computing capacity inside Cordova's run of river Humpback Creek hydroelectric facility.
claims.verbatim: Greensparc delivered a 170-kilowatt computing capacity directly inside Cordova's run-of-river Humpback Creek hydroelectric facility, several miles north of town.
claims.notes: Use 170 kW and only 170 kW. Our 2026-07-26 deck recorded 150 kW and no page fetched this run carries that figure. Attribute as the National Laboratory of the Rockies reported in March. Author Connor O'Neil.

claims.claim: In 2025 hydropower provided more than 83 percent of Cordova's overall electrical demand.
claims.verbatim: In 2025, hydropower provided more than 83% of Cordova's overall electrical demand
claims.notes: The year is load bearing. Write in 2025 and not a bare present tense.

claims.claim: Clay Koplin estimates that 20 to 25 percent of Cordova's hydropower goes unused each year.
claims.verbatim: Koplin estimates that 20%-25% of hydropower goes unused annually.
claims.notes: UNIT WARNING. A percentage OF HYDROPOWER, not of total demand and not of total generation. It is a utility CEO estimate, not a metered published figure, so write Koplin estimates. The source printed an en dash in the range and reader copy must write 20 to 25 percent.

claims.claim: Cordova has about 2,600 residents.
claims.verbatim: its 2,600 remote residents and robust fishing industry
claims.notes: A lab article is not a census source, so write about 2,600. Single sourced.

claims.claim: Clay Koplin said the server was literally 20 feet from the generators.
claims.verbatim: The server was literally 20 feet from the generators. It's designed as a super-energy-efficient deployment.
claims.notes: CONFIRMED as a direct quotation, not a paraphrase. Safe to set in quotation marks on a slide.

claims.claim: Clay Koplin is chief executive officer of Cordova Electric Cooperative.
claims.verbatim: said Clay Koplin, CEO of Cordova Electric Cooperative
claims.notes: Exact title confirmed as CEO.

claims.claim: The Department of Energy and Cordova incrementally developed a smart microgrid from 2017 to 2023.
claims.verbatim: From 2017 to 2023, the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) and Cordova incrementally developed a smart microgrid
claims.notes: The federal money arriving now lands on work that started nine years ago.

claims.claim: A digital twin of Cordova's microgrid was built by the National Laboratory of the Rockies alongside Idaho National Laboratory, Pacific Northwest National Laboratory and Sandia National Laboratories.
claims.verbatim: the team used a digital twin of Cordova's microgrid built by the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) alongside Idaho National Laboratory, Pacific Northwest National Laboratory, and Sandia National Laboratories.
claims.notes: Named on the page as NLR's Advanced Research on Integrated Energy Systems platform.

claims.claim: Greensparc is the edge data center provider that installed the computing on the floor of the Cordova power station.
claims.verbatim: Sam Enoka and Clay Koplin install Greensparc's edge data center on the floor of the Cordova power station
claims.notes: The verbatim is a photo caption rather than body prose, which is why confidence sits below the body sourced claims.

claims.claim: Cordova Electric Cooperative serves 1,566 customers.
claims.verbatim: 1,566 customers
claims.notes: The utility's own about page, fetched this run. No revision date on the page, so date_of_source is the fetch date.

claims.claim: Cordova Electric Cooperative has a generating capacity of 18 megawatts.
claims.verbatim: Generating capacity of 18 megawatts
claims.notes: MAGNITUDE CHECK PASSES. The utility's own plant list gives Orca diesel 10.8 MW, Power Creek hydro 6.0 MW and Humpback Creek hydro 1.25 MW, summing to 18.05 MW.

claims.claim: Cordova is not connected to the State Highway System and Cordova Electric Cooperative is not connected by transmission line to other communities.
claims.value: no transmission line to other communities
claims.verbatim: Cordova is not connected to the State Highway System, and CEC is not connected by transmission line to other communities.
claims.notes: THE LOAD BEARING FACT, verified in the utility's own words rather than inferred. It is what makes Cordova a true islanded microgrid and what makes the surplus unsellable.

claims.claim: The Department of Energy renamed the National Renewable Energy Laboratory the National Laboratory of the Rockies effective December 1st, 2025.
claims.verbatim: The U.S. Department of Energy today renamed the National Renewable Energy Laboratory (NREL) the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR). The renaming is effective immediately
claims.notes: Background, needed only so a reader who knows NREL does not read the partner list as an error.

claims.claim: Alaska DNR has preliminarily decided to authorize a 50 year lease of 715.4 acres to STAK Energy Corporation about 26 miles south of Deadhorse.
claims.verbatim: 715.4 acre parcel located within Sections 1-4, 9-12, and 13-16, Range 13E, Township 6N
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Department of Natural Resources Division of Oil and Gas
claims.notes: Primary state notice, ADL 422741.

claims.claim: The public comment period on the STAK Energy lease closed at 4:30 p.m. Alaska Daylight Time on July 17th, 2026.
claims.verbatim: no later than 4:30 PM Alaska Daylight Time on July 17, 2026
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Department of Natural Resources Division of Oil and Gas
claims.notes: Closed 26 days before this run. Write it in the past tense.

claims.claim: The STAK Energy lease notice is a preliminary decision and no final finding and decision has been published.
claims.verbatim: The Alaska Department of Natural Resources Division of Oil and Gas has preliminarily decided to authorize a 50-year lease to STAK Energy Corporation
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Department of Natural Resources Division of Oil and Gas
claims.notes: Absence of evidence rather than a confirmed negative. Write no final decision has been published, not the state has not decided.

claims.claim: The state notice describes the STAK Energy campus as a commercial natural gas powered energy facility with on site natural gas power generation infrastructure, so its electricity would be generated for itself rather than drawn from an existing Alaska utility grid.
claims.verbatim: commercial natural gas-powered energy facility
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Department of Natural Resources Division of Oil and Gas
claims.notes: THE FAIRNESS GUARD. Any slide putting the North Slope proposal beside Cordova must carry the distinction in the same frame. Proposed and self generated on North Slope gas behind its own meter, against 170 kW operating on a village hydro microgrid in Prince William Sound. Not the same grid, not the same basin, not competing for the same electrons.

claims.claim: Exactly one of the 278 rows on the Department of Energy's Genesis Mission awards list is an Alaska institution, the University of Alaska Fairbanks project AURORA-AI led by Richard Wies.
claims.verbatim: Wies, Richard AURORA-AI: Alaska Utility Resilience & Optimization using Real-time AI University of Alaska Fairbanks  Fairbanks  AK 99775-7880
claims.notes: ADDED BY THE SHOWRUNNER AFTER THE FACT-CHECKER RETURNED, because a treatment-director noticed that the brief called AURORA-AI the single Alaska project and no claim id supported it. Re-verified this run rather than inherited. The PDF was downloaded (HTTP 200, 299,518 bytes, 10 pages, byte-identical in size to the copy run 2026-07-30 pulled) and its text extracted with pypdf. A regex over state-plus-ZIP pairs returns 278 rows, which matches the 278 of C11 from a different source, and a count of state codes returns AK exactly once. ZIP 99775 is the UAF campus ZIP, an internal consistency check. Reproducible by re-running the extraction.

killed.claim: STAK Energy proposes 1 to 3 gigawatts of on site natural gas fired generation for its North Slope campus.
killed.why: Advocacy sourced only. The figure appears on northern.org and the primary DNR notice contains no gigawatt or megawatt figure at all. The underlying state PDFs returned 404 on the direct paths and raw binary on the working paths, and no PDF text tool is installed in this environment. stakenergy.com returned no content, alaskabeacon.com returned 403. No non advocacy source reachable. The deck must not print a gigawatt number.

killed.claim: The STAK Energy campus could consume roughly 350 to 500 million standard cubic feet of gas a day.
killed.why: Same failure path. Attributed by northern.org to an attachment on the state notice that could not be opened. A figure quoted by an advocacy group from a document nobody could read is not verified.

killed.claim: The Genesis Mission first round awarded $293 million across 278 selected projects.
killed.why: Misattribution. The string 293 does not appear in the body of the July 22nd selection announcement, only as anchor text linking to a separate March 17th article where $293 million is the size of the Request for Application, an open funding opportunity rather than the sum of the awards. Replaced by C15.

killed.claim: The Cordova data center has 150 kilowatts of computing capacity.
killed.why: Superseded and unsupported. The string 150 kilowatts is absent from the NLR article and from every page fetched this run. Greensparc publishes no capacity figure and cordovaelectric.com does not mention the data center. Use C18, 170 kW, dated 2026-03-05.

killed.claim: Cordova Electric Cooperative supplies the real world utility operating data for AURORA-AI.
killed.why: Plausible and probably true, and not confirmable verbatim on either release. Both pages name Cordova Electric Cooperative as a partner and nothing more. Asserting the role would be inference dressed as sourcing. Say named project partner, which is C04.

killed.claim: Richard Wies is a professor at UAF's Alaska Center for Energy and Power.
killed.why: Partially killed. The extractable verbatim stops at principal investigator for the project and a professor. The department attachment appeared only in a summarising pass. Use principal investigator on any slide.

killed.claim: A second Richard Wies quotation about bringing AI together with decades of real world utility data.
killed.why: Could not be reproduced character for character on a second pass. House rule is that a named person's quotation must appear verbatim on a fetched page.

killed.claim: Cordova's population is 2,600 per an official census source.
killed.why: Downgraded rather than killed, see C21. The only source reached is a national laboratory feature article, which is not a population authority. Kept at low confidence with about.
